issues.description: push_error called with string but expects ErrorFrame
issues.detail: push_error is a FrameProcessor method that takes an ErrorFrame object, not a keyword string. Calling `self.push_error(error_msg=...)` will raise TypeError unless this service overrides it. The original code had the same bug, but this PR expands the surface area. Verify the signature before merge.

issues.description: Lost error-type context in logs and pushed errors
issues.detail: The refactor collapsed per-type logging (`logger.error(f"ElevenLabs auth error...")`, `Quota exceeded:` prefix) into a single generic `Error:` prefix. Operators previously could grep for auth_error vs quota_exceeded in logs; now they all surface identically. Include the message_type in the pushed error and log line for debuggability.

The error message_type tuple lists `"transcriber_error"` twice (lines 728 and 731). Harmless at runtime but indicates a copy-paste error during review and suggests the list wasn't carefully cross-checked against the ElevenLabs docs. Deduplicate and double-check no documented error type is missing.

issues.description: Silent swallowing of non-connection exceptions removed
issues.detail: Previously `_receive_messages` caught all exceptions from `_process_messages` and logged a warning, so transient parse/handler errors didn't kill the receive loop. Now any exception escaping `_process_response` (e.g., a downstream handler bug) will propagate out, terminating the task and likely triggering websocket_service reconnect behavior. Confirm this is the intended escalation path.

`changelog/3233.fixed.md` has `\ No newline at end of file`. Minor style nit but most repos enforce POSIX text files end with newline; some changelog tooling concatenates these files and a missing newline can merge two bullets onto one line.

issues.description: Stray orphan comment after removed code block
issues.detail: The comment `# Connection closed, will reconnect on next audio chunk` (line 703) now dangles after the except block at indentation that no longer matches its original context. It's still inside the `except Exception` clause for JSON processing, which is misleading — the comment originally referred to the outer connection-closed handler that was removed.

review.summary: The PR correctly identifies a real bug — the inner try/except in `_receive_messages` masks websocket disconnects from the outer reconnect loop — and the fix (removing the swallowing wrapper) is sound. However, the error-handling expansion loses per-type context in both logs and pushed errors, contains a duplicated `transcriber_error` entry, and may have a latent `push_error` signature issue worth verifying. A stray comment and missing newline are cosmetic. Overall direction is good; tighten error reporting and dedupe before merge.
